label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 18:51:53Z ledger-consumer was redeployed with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, a handler that does not deduplicate by event_id. The provider resends a webhook until it is acknowledged, so one event can land on provider-events several times, as separate messages at different offsets. The naive handler books every copy: 6 events twice, evt_000308 three times. The extra payment postings push the ledger above the provider. The extra refund posting (evt_000288, pay_000217) pushes it below for that payment. Net: the ledger is +$493.23 ahead. The ledger stays balanced because each duplicate is a full double-entry transaction. Still open: why redeliveries are this frequent. It could be normal provider retries or slow acks from webhook-receiver; I did not check. Either way, the handler must deduplicate.

evidence.shows: posted_exactly_once failed: 7 events posted 2 or 3 times (6 payment.succeeded, 1 refund.succeeded). matches_provider is off by +$493.23, and each per-payment difference equals one extra copy of the event amount. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 18:51:53Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, 17s before the alert. It is the only service deployed after the 18:50:26 stack start.
evt_000308 (pay_000279, 13193 cents) was booked three times, from different offsets 0@100, 0@101 and 0@103. Each redelivered copy was posted without a duplicate check.
Both postings of evt_000251 came after the redeploy: 18:51:53.668 from offset 2@73 and 18:51:54.680 from offset 2@76. The duplicates began with the naive handler.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its previous LEDGER_HANDLER setting, which should be the handler that dedupes by event_id, so it stops booking redelivered events. Then repair the data: reverse the extra ledger transactions for the 7 duplicated events and keep the first posting of each. That means evt_000251 txn 255, evt_000261 txn 266, evt_000267 txn 272, evt_000268 txn 273, evt_000288 txn 297, plus the extra transactions for evt_000298 and evt_000308. Finally, rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses briefly while its container is recreated, so ledger booking lags for that time. Kafka retains the events, so none are lost. The rollback does not remove the duplicates already booked; that needs a separate data repair. If the previous setting is not a deduplicating handler, the duplicates will continue.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, its current setting in the deploy log. This is not recommended, because it brings back the double-booking.
